:::{#rem-matrix-entries}
#### Matrix entries, and vectors as matrices

The entry in row $i$ and column $j$ of $\matr{A}$ is written $a_{ij}$
or $(\matr{A})_{ij}$.
For example, for the $2 \times 3$ matrix

$$
\matr{A} =
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 2 & 3 \\
4 & 5 & 6
\end{bmatrix},
$$

$a_{12} = 2$ and $a_{23} = 6$.

A column vector of length $p$ is a $p \times 1$ matrix,
and a row vector of length $p$ is a $1 \times p$ matrix.
For example, $(2, -1, 5)$ is a $3 \times 1$ matrix,
and its transpose $[2,\; -1,\; 5]$ is a $1 \times 3$ matrix.

:::
